scope: Inference request lifetime, CPU context preparation, SSE parsing, engine version/status probes and startup health deadline
summary_ja: 生成条件を変更せず、取消の伝播漏れ、通信スレッド上のcontext計算、SSEの繰り返しコピー/再解析、状態確認の重複プロセス起動、起動期限を超えるhealth待ちを修正。速度倍率ではなく失敗の解消と処理回数で検証。

concepts: ChannelServer.onPromise ties request disposal to cancellation

reference.adaptation: Apply request-lifetime cancellation and bounded work to the existing Rust daemon and external engine process; no VS Code runtime or editor transplant.

environment.engines: Loopback HTTP stand-ins, shell child processes and minimal fixture model headers

cancellation.baseline: Unmodified phase 2 source; only the new test file was copied into the comparison checkout.

cases.condition: Abort the generation future after the stand-in engine accepts the request, before any decoded event.
Read one decoded event, then drop the returned stream while the engine remains silent.
Send a complete HTTP request through the real Studio router, then close the TCP connection before response headers.
Read the first content event through the real SSE endpoint, then drop the HTTP response.

cancellation.deadline_interpretation: A regression-test failure deadline, not a measured UI or inference latency. No speed ratio is derived from it.
implementation: The state forwarding task selects receiver.closed() as well as the next backend event.
The bounded backend producer's entire future is cancelled when its receiver closes, including quiet reads and retries.
Generation metrics have a Drop guard so cancellation before the forwarding task starts cannot leak an active generation.

conditions: Dropping a stream releases a producer waiting without sending.
A stream dropped before its scheduled task runs produces zero events.
A consumer that never polls allows exactly 32 successful channel sends; dropping it releases the blocked producer.
backend_producer_regressions.constraint: The channel limit counts events, not bytes.

conditions.input: 2048 repetitions of mixed Japanese, emoji and ASCII text, delivered one byte at a time

conditions.assertion: All content events plus a split Japanese reasoning event remain ordered; bytes after DONE are ignored.
Each frame is inspected once; a claim ID with committed=false remains uncommitted.

changes: Scan only newly appended bytes of an unfinished line.
Compact the SSE byte buffer once per received chunk instead of draining/copying the suffix for every line.
Read gateway receipt metadata in the existing JSON parse; remove the growing whole-response tail and its repeated reparsing.
sse_regressions.constraint: The largest unfinished SSE line still requires buffering; this does not impose a new payload-size limit.

conditions: CPU context work can remain occupied while the single-thread async executor continues running.
Cancelling a request waiting for a worker slot performs zero context jobs.
A cancelled job that has already started retains its slot until its CPU work ends.
Dropping a request also aborts a job still queued inside Tokio's blocking pool.
integration: Context plan, finish and required-input compaction execute in the bounded blocking pool.
The original conversation is shared with Arc rather than copied into a worker on the HTTP executor.
Context preview uses the same helper.
Hardware discovery and initial metrics construction run outside the async executor.
constraints: A native tokenizer call already executing is not preempted; its result is discarded after request cancellation and its worker permit remains held until return.
HTTP disconnect propagation and context-queue cancellation are separately tested; no claim is made that an executing tokenizer is forcibly stopped.
The context-selection algorithm, tokenizer, summarizer sampling and generation sampling are unchanged.

version_probe_regressions.invalidation: Executable mtime or size changes invalidate cached status; the short TTL also bounds changes with an unchanged stamp.
version_probe_regressions.provenance_policy: descriptor() serializes with the same probe lock but always bypasses cached output and performs a fresh probe for the load.
version_probe_regressions.child_lifetime: kill_on_drop is enabled for version-only subprocesses; both timeout and cancelled awaiters terminate them.
constraints: The TTL is not a permanent availability cache.
The 30-second ceiling is a configured subprocess timeout, not a latency measurement.
Descriptor freshness preserves the existing external-binary provenance model; the cache does not claim binary identity beyond the engine's reported banner.

configurations: HTTP 200 headers received, JSON body never completes
asserted: Both loads return the existing startup-timeout error.
The second request starts after the first timeout, rather than remaining stuck in the model-load queue.
Both timed-out child processes are reaped.
The model-load lock is free and no model is marked loaded.
startup_health_regression.production_behavior: The existing startup deadline covers the HTTP header and body awaits, and polling sleeps use only the remaining budget. No additional wait setting was introduced.
startup_health_regression.constraint: The fixture budget tests termination behavior; it is not a real-model load-time measurement.

checkpoints.scope: Runtime library immediately after cancellation/context/SSE changes
checkpoints.ignored_reason: Existing opt-in live testnet-12 preflight test

checkpoints.scope: OpenAI child suite after version cache additions
Health deadline and model-load queue regression after the final source change

reporting_limits: No real GPU token-throughput, first-token latency or UI paint/interaction benchmark was run for these changes.
Before/after comparison demonstrates cancellation failures being fixed; no millisecond multiplier is reported.
Process counts, event counts, parse counts, queue bounds and preserved behavior are the measured/asserted outcomes.
The root's final full test, Clippy and release-build gates are separate from these task checkpoints.
